title: Weighted periodic-orbit zeta function
notes: The notes define \(\zeta_T(z,\varphi)=\exp\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{z^n}{n}\sum_{\xi\in\operatorname{Fix}T^n}\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}\varphi(T^kx)\).
statement: If every fixed-point set is finite, the same formula with \(x=\xi\) defines a formal series. It defines a holomorphic germ when its weighted fixed-point sums grow at most exponentially. The product contains exactly \(n\) factors.
reconstruction: The bound for convergence and the correction of the dummy variable are explicit additions. No global continuation is claimed from the definition alone.
fate: The bibliographical pointer is \citet[abstract, pp.~105--115]{mayer1987location}, published in August 1987 before this report; it places the definition in an already established thermodynamic-formalism setting. The reporter is not identified as Mayer.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The weighted periodic-orbit definition is established; analytic continuation depends on the dynamical and function-space hypotheses, and does not follow merely from the displayed formal series.

title: A quotient of transfer-operator Fredholm determinants
notes: For a full-branch piecewise linear interval map the notes write \(\zeta_T=\det(1-zL_1)/\det(1-zL_2)\), with \(L_1f=\varphi\sum_j\rho_j^{-1}f\circ\psi_j\) and \(L_2f=\varphi\sum_jf\circ\psi_j\).
statement: One precise version assumes finitely many holomorphic contracting inverse branches \(\psi_j\) on a complex domain, holomorphic weights, and a holomorphic function space on which the induced operators are nuclear and satisfy the fixed-point trace formula. Put \(L_1f(w)=\sum_j\psi_j\prime(w)\varphi(w)f(\psi_jw)\), \(L_2f(w)=\sum_j\varphi(w)f(\psi_jw)\). For affine branches, subtraction of the two fixed-point traces gives the weighted periodic-orbit sum, hence the displayed determinant quotient near zero and by continuation. Periodic endpoint multiplicities must follow the chosen coding.
reconstruction: The analytic setting, signed derivative \(\psi_j\prime\), and boundary convention are supplied. Keeping \(\varphi(w)\) outside the sum is compatible with the cyclic product along periodic orbits. A pole-location theorem itself is not stated in the notebook.
fate: \citet[abstract]{mayer1987location} explicitly uses nuclear operators on holomorphic Banach spaces. Only that abstract and metadata were read; the precise model stated here is a reconstruction using the trace identity, not a claim that every hypothesis was read in Mayer\textquotesingle s text.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Established in analytic transfer-operator settings. The unrestricted interval-map statement is incomplete, and the title about pole location is not enough evidence for a theorem that all poles are real.

title: Finite-type shift and periodic-point counts
notes: The alphabet \(F\), allowed neighbour pairs \(M\subset F\times F\), bi-infinite admissible sequences and the shift \(T\) are defined. The adjacency operator is then introduced.
statement: For the zero-one adjacency matrix \(A\) of a finite directed graph, the two-sided edge-admissible shift has \(N_n=\#\operatorname{Fix}(T^n)=\operatorname{tr}(A^n)\). The trace counts closed walks with a distinguished starting position, exactly as fixed sequences are counted.
fate: This is the finite-matrix part of the dynamical-zeta theory already underlying the references of \citet{mayer1987location}. Its proof is the elementary closed-walk count written in the notes.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The count is exact for finite alphabets; no mixing, irreducibility, or aperiodicity is needed.

title: Rationality of the zeta function of a finite-state shift
notes: The speaker derives \(\zeta_T(s)=\det(1-sA)^{-1}\) from \(N_n=\operatorname{tr}A^n\), initially for \(|s|<1/\#F\).
statement: For every finite square matrix \(A\), \(\exp(\sum_{n\ge1}\operatorname{tr}(A^n)s^n/n)=\det(I-sA)^{-1}\) as a formal series, hence as analytic germs. For a zero-one \(m\)-state shift, \(|s|<1/m\) is a sufficient convergence disk; the rational expression continues meromorphically to the whole complex plane.
fate: The source itself supplies the trace-log argument; the finite-state case predates the analytic-transfer work cited in \citet{mayer1987location}.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Completely settled; the convergence bound in the notebook need not be optimal.

title: Single-eigenvalue constraints for a stochastic matrix
notes: Gelfand recalls that a stochastic matrix has eigenvalue \(1\) and spectrum in the unit disk, and mentions work of Dynkin and Dmitriev on the possible position of an individual eigenvalue.
statement: For a real row-stochastic \(n\times n\) matrix \(P\), \(P\mathbf1=\mathbf1\) and \(\rho(P)\le\|P\|_\infty=1\); nonreal eigenvalues occur in conjugate pairs. Determining the union of possible individual eigenvalues projects away all correlations between eigenvalues and is a different question from realizing a whole multiset.
fate: The elementary bound follows directly from the stated stochastic hypotheses. The exact single-eigenvalue region was determined by \citet{karpelevich1951roots}; its opened record confirms publication in1951, received19May1950. The source attribution to Dynkin and Dmitriev concerns earlier work and is retained. The joint problem is assessed separately in item1987-728.4.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: These elementary necessary conditions are known and are far from a sufficient joint-spectrum criterion.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: All eigenvalues of a stochastic matrix simultaneously
notes: Gelfand expressly asks for the region of complete eigenvalue lists in \(\mathbb C^n\), emphasizing that the known plane region describes only its projection. The Russian marks this \ru{Задача!!}.
statement: For each fixed \(n\), characterize the multisets \(\Lambda=(1,\lambda_2,\ldots,\lambda_n)\) for which a real matrix \(P\ge0\), \(P\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), has characteristic polynomial \(\prod_{j=1}^n(t-\lambda_j)\). Multiplicity is algebraic; reducible and non-diagonalizable matrices are allowed. No doubly stochastic, symmetry or prescribed-zero-pattern condition is imposed.
fate: This is the stochastic inverse eigenvalue problem, rather than the one-eigenvalue region. The chapter\textquotesingle s development and its exact literature comparison give low-dimensional realizations, necessary moment inequalities and the unresolved general obstruction.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The general fixed-size joint realization problem remains only partially characterized. The chapter settles the stated low-dimensional subcases, without claiming a criterion for arbitrary lists or arbitrary n.
worth: A bounded development is worthwhile because exact small-dimensional realizations and explicit moment obstructions sharpen the distinction the notes make between a spectral projection and a full spectrum.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Finite-memory weights reduce to a finite matrix
notes: The speaker replaces the alphabet by admissible blocks of length \(k\), gives the overlap transition rule, and obtains \(\zeta_T(s,\varphi)=\det(I-sL)^{-1}\). The orbit product in this page is printed with upper limit \(n\).
statement: If \(\varphi\) depends on \(k\) consecutive symbols, let \(L_{\alpha\beta}=\varphi(\alpha)\) when the admissible blocks overlap and concatenate, and zero otherwise. Then \(\operatorname{tr}L^n\) is the sum of \(\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}\varphi(T^jx)\) over period-n fixed sequences, and the weighted zeta function is \(\det(I-sL)^{-1}\).
reconstruction: The upper bound is corrected from n to n-1, as required by the stated transition matrix; no arbitrary long-range potential is covered.
fate: This is the same finite-dimensional trace-log identity as item 1987-728.2, applied to the higher-block presentation; it is expository material in the transfer-operator setting of \citet{mayer1987location}.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The corrected finite-memory theorem is exact. The literal product of n+1 weights is false: for a one-symbol shift of constant weight c it gives \((1-sc)^{-c}\), rather than \((1-sc)^{-1}\).

title: The rational product formula and p-adic arithmetic
notes: After Gelfand urges the audience to learn p-adic arithmetic and root extraction, Beilinson writes \(\prod_v|a|_v=1\), with \(a\in\mathbb Q\), and checks \(a=1/2\).
statement: For \(a\in\mathbb Q^\times\), normalize \(|p|_p=p^{-1}\) and take the usual real absolute value. Then \(|a|_\infty\prod_p|a|_p=1\), with only finitely many nonunit factors. Learning root extraction means solving equations when solutions exist; it does not assert that \(\mathbb Q_p\) is algebraically closed.
reconstruction: The nonzero hypothesis and normalization are supplied.
fate: The product formula and the adelic measure framework are classical; \citet[Chapters~I--II]{serre1981adeles} predates the talk. The displayed example follows immediately from the valuation of 2.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The theorem is exact after excluding a=0. No new assertion that arbitrary p-adic elements admit every root is attributed to Gelfand.

title: Completed zeta functional equation and a wrong power of pi
notes: Equation (2) is the completed Riemann zeta functional equation. Equation (3) rewrites it with a factor \(\pi^{1-s}\) and an Euler product, explicitly saying analytic continuation is understood.
statement: With \(\Lambda(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\), one has \(\Lambda(s)=\Lambda(1-s)\) meromorphically. Consequently \(\zeta(1-s)/\zeta(s)=\pi^{1/2-s}\Gamma(s/2)/\Gamma((1-s)/2)\), wherever the quotient is defined and then by meromorphic continuation. The formal product \(\prod_p(1-p^{-s})/(1-p^{s-1})\) is not a pair of ordinarily convergent Euler products on any common half-plane.
reconstruction: The gamma ratio is corrected by direct division of equation (2).
fate: \citet[25.4.3--25.4.4]{nist2026dlmf} gives the established symmetric equation. The notes\textquotesingle exponent follows neither from it nor from a change of gamma convention.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The equation is classical; the exponent 1-s is a faithful notebook error and must be 1/2-s. Analytic continuation, explicitly mentioned in the source, remains essential.

title: Adelic factorization of string amplitudes
notes: The gamma ratio is described as approximately an open-string Veneziano--Witten amplitude, with a product over primes. Three recent papers are named: Volovich, Manin, and Witten with an unnamed coauthor.
statement: The identifiable reference is Freund--Witten\textquotesingle s factorization of appropriate four-particle open- and closed-string amplitudes into p-adic factors, after analytic continuation and normalization. The single-variable gamma ratio displayed here is an illustrative specialization; it does not specify the full three Mandelstam variables, on-shell constraint, or normalization of a complete amplitude.
reconstruction: The amplitude identification comes from the named topic and opened abstract; no missing multivariable formula is attributed to the speaker.
fate: \citet[abstract]{freundwitten1987adelic} identifies the missing coauthor and states the Veneziano and Virasoro--Shapiro product relations. Journal publication was 17 December 1987, ten days after the seminar; the report itself is evidence of earlier circulation. Only metadata and abstract were read.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The particular paper is identified with high confidence. The notebook\textquotesingle s schematic one-variable expression is only a partial match to its complete amplitude formulas.

title: Tamagawa volume of SL(n) and the real lattice covolume
notes: The shorthand \ru{Мера Тамагавы = 1} is expanded into \(\operatorname{vol}(SL_n(\mathbb A)/SL_n(\mathbb Q))=1\) and \(\operatorname{vol}(SL_n(\mathbb R)/SL_n(\mathbb Z))=\prod_{j=2}^n\zeta(j)\).
statement: For \(n\ge2\), use the restricted adelic product and Tamagawa Haar measures from a rational invariant top form. Then \(\tau(SL_n)=1\). With compatible real and p-adic normalization and \(\operatorname{vol}(SL_n(\mathbb Z_p))=\prod_{j=2}^n(1-p^{-j})\), strong approximation gives the stated real covolume. Replacing Haar measure by an arbitrary scalar multiple changes that covolume.
reconstruction: The restricted product, quotient, and common normalization are made explicit.
fate: These are classical volume calculations; \citet[Chapters~II--III, especially the contents at pp.~122 and 180]{serre1981adeles} records the relevant pre-1987 framework. Full scan access exceeded the reader limit, so verification is metadata, not a claim to have read its proof.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The normalized theorem is settled. The statement concerns the volume of an arithmetic quotient, not the total measure of the group or an unnormalized Haar measure.

title: The SL(2) volume picture on the hyperbolic plane
notes: The notes identify \(SL_2(\mathbb R)\) with disk automorphisms and use hyperbolic area times an angular measure on \(S^*H^2\).
statement: Orientation-preserving hyperbolic-plane isometries form \(PSL_2(\mathbb R)=SL_2(\mathbb R)/\{\pm I\}\); they act simply transitively on oriented unit tangent frames. Hyperbolic area times fibre-angle measure is Haar measure on this frame group. Lifting it to \(SL_2\) requires accounting for the double cover before comparing with the Tamagawa normalization.
reconstruction: The central quotient and double-cover normalization are supplied.
fate: The construction is classical and illustrates the arithmetic-volume calculation of item 1987-729.4; see the real-measure and arithmetic-group sections listed in \citet{serre1981adeles}.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The geometric model is valid after distinguishing SL from PSL and fixing the angular period. It alone does not select the normalization giving zeta(2).

title: Counting GL(n) and SL(n) over a finite field
notes: The audience is asked to count \(SL_n(\mathbb F_p)\); the next page counts successively independent columns of \(GL_n\) and divides by \(p-1\).
statement: For a prime power \(q\), \(\#GL_n(\mathbb F_q)=\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}(q^n-q^i)\), because each new column must avoid the span of its predecessors. The surjective determinant map has equally sized fibres, so \(\#SL_n=\#GL_n/(q-1)=q^{n^2-1}\prod_{j=2}^n(1-q^{-j})\).
fate: The argument is fully present in the source and belongs to the classical-group point counts listed at p.~20 of \citet{serre1981adeles}.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The formula is exact, including n=1 with the empty product. It supplies the local factors used in the previous volume formula.

title: An adelic volume analogy for moduli of curves
notes: Manin is credited with an analogous formula for a moduli-space volume; Gelfand asks what p-adic volume and an adelic Teichmuller space would mean.
statement: No precise moduli functor, genus, marked-point data, differential form or measure normalization, convergence condition, or equation is given. The strongest supported content is a request to formulate an adelic analogue of the preceding volume comparison.
fate: Searches for Manin\textquotesingle s arithmetical-physics reflections identify a contemporaneous programme, but neither the notebook nor the accessible bibliographic records supplies an exact conjecture to match. The explicit amplitude relation of \citet{freundwitten1987adelic} concerns a different, specified object.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: No definite statement can be assigned a solved or open status from these notes. Later p-adic moduli and string constructions do not by themselves identify this particular question.

title: Fourier transformation moves local information to infinity
notes: A compactly supported generalized function on the line is Fourier transformed to a smooth function; the notes say its singularities become asymptotic behaviour at infinity, then mention Laumon\textquotesingle s use of Witten\textquotesingle s Morse-theoretic ideas.
statement: For \(u\in\mathcal E\prime(\mathbb R)\), \(\widehat u(z)=\langle u(x),e^{-izx}\rangle\) is entire of exponential type and of polynomial growth on the real axis. Smoothness and singular support are reflected in directional decay of localized Fourier transforms. A single unspecified asymptotic expansion need not determine every singularity; the full Fourier transform determines u.
reconstruction: The entire extension and localized decay formulation clarify the informal word singularities; they are not asserted to be verbatim in the notes.
fate: \citet[Introduction, pp.~131--134]{laumon1987fourier} explicitly develops the finite-field Fourier analogy and acknowledges Witten\textquotesingle s Morse-theory inspiration. The real-distribution statement is standard background, not a theorem first proved there.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The real Fourier statement is established. Laumon\textquotesingle s arithmetic stationary-phase construction is a precise analogue, not an identification of real distributions with l-adic sheaves.

title: Determinant line of a finite complex
notes: The notes set \(\det H^\bullet=(\det H^0\otimes\det H^2)\otimes(\det H^1)^{-1}\) and assert equality with the analogous determinant of a complex.
statement: For a bounded complex \(C^\bullet\) of finite-dimensional vector spaces, define \(\det C^\bullet=\bigotimes_i(\bigwedge^{\dim C^i}C^i)^{(-1)^i}\). The short exact sequences of boundaries, cycles and cohomology give a natural isomorphism \(\det C^\bullet\simeq\det H^\bullet(C)\), with coherent graded signs. Finiteness or a perfect-complex hypothesis is necessary.
reconstruction: The boundedness, finite-dimensionality and graded-sign conditions are supplied.
fate: The construction was established before the talk in \citet[Section~I]{knudsenmumford1976det}; the opened author-hosted scan confirms the publication, while the exact finite-dimensional isomorphism is also obtained directly from the two short exact sequences.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Standard determinant-functor theory. This valid isomorphism must be separated from the following divisor formula, whose displayed sign is inconsistent.

title: The determinant-divisor formula has the wrong variance
notes: For \(D=\sum a_ix_i\), the notes define \(\det F_D=\bigotimes_i(\det F_{x_i})^{a_i}\), then write \(\det H^\bullet(X,F)=\det F_K\) for the canonical divisor K.
statement: The divisor construction is meaningful for a local system F and a specified divisor. The claimed natural identity with K is false under the immediately preceding alternating determinant convention. For a constant local system V on a compact genus-g curve, automorphisms of V act on \(\det R\Gamma(X,V)\) with determinant weight \(2-2g\), while \(\det V_K\) has weight \(2g-2\). Dualizing the right side removes this elementary sign obstruction, but a canonical general product formula requires additional local epsilon data and conventions.
reconstruction: The comparison of determinant weights is our consistency check. We do not silently replace the source formula by an asserted canonical isomorphism with \(F_{-K}\).
fate: \citet[Section~I]{knudsenmumford1976det} fixes the determinant convention; \citet[Chapter~III, Theorem~3.2.1.1]{laumon1987fourier} proves a precise arithmetic epsilon-product statement, not this unqualified identity of lines.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The literal formula is false functorially. The sign diagnosis is decisive even on a constant sheaf on the projective line; it does not establish a replacement theorem for arbitrary constructible sheaves.

title: Laumon: local factors for global epsilon constants
notes: The discussion of determinants is presented as a report on Laumon\textquotesingle s work in number theory and on a local description of the functional-equation constant.
statement: For a smooth proper curve over a finite field of characteristic p and a constructible l-adic complex, \(l\ne p\), the global epsilon constant of its L-function is expressed as a product of locally defined epsilon factors, with the normalization and genus/rank factor specified by Laumon. A nonzero rational differential supplies the local additive characters; the resulting global expression is independent of that choice. Local Fourier transforms and stationary phase supply the proof.
reconstruction: The arithmetic objects and hypotheses come from the identified paper, while the notebook gives only the motivating outline.
fate: \citet[Theorem~3.2.1.1; Remark~3.2.1.3]{laumon1987fourier} contains the exact product theorem. It was already published in 1987 when Beilinson reported it in December.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Established. The field, coefficient and normalization hypotheses matter: this result cannot be read as a blanket complex-analytic determinant-line formula.

title: Toric varieties, fans, and equivariant vector bundles
notes: The speaker defines a toric variety by an algebraic-torus action with an orbit isomorphic to the torus, associates a fan, and defines a compatible linear action on a vector bundle.
statement: A normal toric variety over an algebraically closed field contains \(T\simeq(\mathbb G_m)^d\) as a dense open orbit, with multiplication extending to the variety. It corresponds to a rational polyhedral fan in \(N_\mathbb R\), where \(N=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb G_m,T)\) is the cocharacter lattice. A toric vector bundle is an algebraic vector bundle equipped with a T-action linear on fibres and covering the base action.
reconstruction: Density, normality and the integral cocharacter structure are supplied.
fate: This is the standard background recalled by \citet[Section~1]{klyachko1989equivariant}. The existence of an orbit merely isomorphic to T is not enough without density and normality.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Established definitions. The combinatorial lattice belongs to one-parameter subgroups, not an arbitrary vector-space identification with the Lie algebra.

title: Klyachko classification by compatible filtrations
notes: An equivariant bundle yields a vector space E and decreasing filtrations \(E^\alpha(i)\), one for each ray. The notes require the subspaces on each cone to generate a distributive lattice.
statement: On a smooth toric variety \(X_\Sigma\), toric vector bundles correspond to finite-dimensional E with exhaustive separated decreasing integer filtrations \(E^\rho(i)\). On every cone \(\sigma\) there must be a decomposition \(E=\bigoplus_{u\in M}E_u\) with \(E^\rho(i)=\sum_{\langle u,v_\rho\rangle\ge i}E_u\) for all rays of that cone. Morphisms preserve every filtration. On a smooth cone simultaneous splitting, equivalently distributivity, supplies such integral characters. For singular cones the integral-character compatibility must be imposed explicitly.
reconstruction: The smooth/singular distinction, finite filtration conditions, character lattice, and morphisms are supplied from the identified theorem.
fate: \citet[Theorems~0.1.1 and 2.2.1]{klyachko1989equivariant} gives the precise equivalence. The paper was received on 3 February 1988, published in Russian in 1989 and translated in 1990; the seminar documents circulation in December 1987.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The theorem is established, including a precise singular version. The raw distributivity criterion without smoothness is incomplete.

title: Recover cohomology and characteristic classes from filtrations
notes: The explicit tasks are to compute cohomology, Chern classes and related geometric quantities from the filtration data.
statement: Given a smooth complete toric variety with fan \(\Sigma\) and a compatible filtered vector space representing \(\mathcal E\), determine the weight spaces of \(H^q(X_\Sigma,\mathcal E)\) and the Chern classes from that finite combinatorial data. Completeness ensures finite-dimensional global cohomology; for a noncomplete variety the characterwise construction still needs the corresponding finiteness interpretation.
reconstruction: Completeness and the precise output invariants are added to make the question finite and testable.
fate: \citet[Theorems~3.2.1, 4.1.1 and 4.2.1]{klyachko1989equivariant} gives Chern-class formulas, a complex computing cohomology and character formulas. Submission February 1988 followed this December 1987 report; publication was 1989/1990.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The stated recovery problem is solved by Klyachko\textquotesingle s constructions. This is not an unsolved request for a new cohomology theory.

title: Classification and moduli of compatible filtration data
notes: The second broad task is classification of the bundles; the speaker then abstracts the compatibility rule to a finite simplicial complex with a filtration at every vertex.
statement: For a fixed complex K, a fixed rank r and prescribed dimensions of the filtration steps, classify the configurations of flags in \(\mathbb C^r\) whose subspaces are simultaneously split on each simplex, modulo simultaneous \(GL_r\). For a toric fan, use the stronger character compatibility when needed. Constructing a parameter space and understanding its orbit equivalence is a precise interpretation of classification; it need not produce a finite list.
reconstruction: Rank, flag dimensions and the quotient problem are supplied; the paper cited solves the toric fixed-data moduli problem, not every possible meaning of classification.
fate: For toric bundles, \citet[Theorem~1.1 and Section~4]{payne2008moduli}, first circulated in May 2007 and published in 2008, constructs framed moduli with fixed equivariant Chern data and proves Murphy\textquotesingle s law already in rank three. This develops the geometric moduli question, while not claiming a simple orbit list for every abstract simplicial complex.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Established moduli constructions and severe singularity phenomena explain the limits of a uniform elementary classification. The arbitrary-complex reformulation remains a representation problem with complexity depending on K, not one unqualified open conjecture.

title: A filled simplex has only one-dimensional split summands
notes: For the triangle, all three filtrations are compatible and the speaker decomposes the representation into one-dimensional ones.
statement: If all filtrations attached to the vertices of a filled simplex are simultaneously split, choose a common basis of E adapted to every filtration. The one-dimensional coordinate lines, endowed with their integer jump positions, give a direct-sum decomposition of the filtered object. This uses a filled simplex; its boundary has weaker compatibility.
reconstruction: The distinction between a filled triangle and its boundary is made explicit.
fate: This is the elementary simultaneous-basis content of the distributivity condition in \citet[Theorem~0.1.1]{klyachko1989equivariant}; no later classification is needed.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The splitting is exact for the stated common-basis condition. It must not be transferred to complexes where only proper faces are constrained.

title: Tetrahedral configurations and the short-filtration restriction
notes: For the boundary of a tetrahedron the notes give four planes in general position in a three-dimensional space, their exterior powers, and assert that all representations split into those and one-dimensional objects.
statement: The matching theorem concerns toric bundles on projective space whose ray filtrations are short: each has at most one proper nonzero subspace, with allowed integer shifts. For \(\mathbb P^3\), such bundles decompose into line bundles and the appropriate twists of exterior powers of its cotangent bundle. Their filtration configurations include the four general-position planes described in the notes. The same conclusion for arbitrary long filtrations does not follow.
reconstruction: The short-filtration hypothesis is taken from the proved theorem. The source does not state it explicitly, so the literal unrestricted assertion is not endorsed.
fate: \citet[Theorem~6.4.1]{klyachko1989equivariant} states the required short-filtration theorem; published1989/1990 after its December1987 exposition. The missing restriction is substantive.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The restricted theorem is established. The unqualified notebook sentence is not a classification of all vector bundles on projective three-space or of all arbitrary-length tetrahedral flag configurations.

title: Isolating tractable pieces of a representation problem
notes: Gelfand urges finding the solvable portions of any classification problem and refers to the ideology of Gelfand--Ponomarev.
statement: The supported content is a methodological recommendation: split direct-sum objects into indecomposables and identify representation-finite or otherwise tractable subclasses before seeking a uniform description. It is not a claim that every classification problem has a computable finite list.
fate: The concrete antecedent is \citet{gelfandponomarev1971quadruples}, already discussed in the earlier index at 1970-198 and 1972-277; the present sheet later explicitly returns to the four-subspace problem.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: A documented methodological link, with no new unsolved mathematical assertion.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Kac: indecomposable dimension vectors are positive roots
notes: The notes connect dimensions at graph vertices to coordinates of roots of a Kac--Moody algebra, mention numbers of parameters, and cite Lecture Notes996 and an earlier Inventiones paper.
statement: For a finite quiver without loops over an algebraically closed field, the dimension vectors of indecomposable representations are exactly the positive roots of the associated symmetric Kac--Moody root system. A positive real root gives a unique indecomposable up to isomorphism. For imaginary roots there can be parameter families; a bare dimension vector does not specify a unique object. The Tits quadratic form controls the parameter count in the precise representation-variety formulation.
reconstruction: The field, quiver and real-versus-imaginary hypotheses are supplied, and no unverified universal moduli-dimension formula is substituted for the shorthand.
fate: The exact volume cited is \citet[pp.~74--108]{kac1983roots}, published in1983 and listed on Kac\textquotesingle s own bibliography. The linked scan was too large to read here; verification is limited to identification and metadata.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Kac\textquotesingle s root theorem is established and predates the talk. It classifies dimension vectors and real-root objects, not every imaginary-root isomorphism class by a single root.

title: Evaluate Cauchy's determinant
notes: Problem1 asks for \(\det(1/(x_i-y_j))\).
statement: If \(x_i\ne y_j\) for every i,j, then \[\det_{1\le i,j\le n}\frac1{x_i-y_j}=\frac{\prod_{i<j}(x_j-x_i)(y_i-y_j)}{\prod_{i,j}(x_i-y_j)}.\] Repeated x or y values give zero, consistently with the formula.
fate: This is the classical double alternant, checked in \citet[Section~2.1, equation~(2.7)]{krattenthaler1999determinant}; his1999 exposition is not the first publication. It recurs from item1981-541.3 in the earlier index.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Solved before the seminar. The difference-denominator sign is included explicitly.

title: Real roots of the Rodrigues polynomial
notes: Problem2 asks to prove that the nth derivative of \((x^2-1)^n\) has only real roots.
statement: For every integer \(n\ge1\), \(\frac{d^n}{dx^n}(x^2-1)^n=2^nn!P_n(x)\), where \(P_n\) is the Legendre polynomial. It has exactly n simple roots, all in \((-1,1)\). Repeated Rolle arguments applied to the endpoint roots of multiplicity n already prove the required reality.
fate: The Rodrigues formula and orthogonal-polynomial zero theorem are recorded in \citet[18.5(ii),18.2(vi)]{nist2026dlmf}; item1968-160.15 records the earlier seminar connection.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Solved classical exercise. n=0 gives a nonzero constant and no roots.

title: Discontinuities of a pointwise limit of continuous functions
notes: Problem3 asks whether a pointwise limit on an interval can be discontinuous, have a dense set of discontinuities, or be discontinuous everywhere.
statement: A real-valued pointwise limit of continuous functions on a nondegenerate real interval is Baire class1 and has a dense G-delta set of continuity points. It may be discontinuous (for example \(x^n\) on \([0,1]\)), and discontinuities may be dense (Thomae\textquotesingle s function, with value \(1/q\) at a reduced rational \(p/q\) and0 at irrationals). It cannot be discontinuous everywhere.
fate: \citet[p.~173, theorem and reference to the1899 thesis]{baire1900nouvelle} provides the classical criterion for pointwise continuous approximation. The category conclusion applies to interval domains, which are Baire spaces.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: All three questions are settled: yes, yes, no. Pointwise convergence must not be replaced by uniform convergence.

title: Conformally map the radially slit disk
notes: Problem4(a) draws a disk cut along a radius and asks for a conformal map to a disk.
statement: For \(\Omega=\{z:|z|<1\}\setminus[0,1)\), choose \(w=\sqrt z\) with \(0<\arg z<2\pi\). Then w maps onto the upper half-disk; \(h=(1+w)/(1-w)\) maps that onto the first quadrant. Therefore \(f(z)=(h^2-i)/(h^2+i)\) is a biholomorphism from \(\Omega\) to the unit disk. A rotated slit is treated by an initial rotation.
reconstruction: The unit radius and positive-real slit choose coordinates for the picture; the construction is supplied here.
fate: The existence is a classical case of the mapping theorem originating in \citet[pp.~37--39 of the checked transcription]{riemann1851grundlagen}. The elementary displayed composition is an annotation of the exercise, not a formula found in the notebook.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Solved. The slit endpoint0 is removed, so no normalization f(0)=0 is imposed.

title: Conformally map the dumbbell domain with a thin corridor
notes: Problem4(b) draws two unit disks joined by a corridor of width \(10^{-6}\), marks A at a disk centre, and asks for a disk map sending A to0.
statement: If the drawn union is an open connected simply connected proper plane domain \(\Omega\) and \(A\in\Omega\), the Riemann mapping theorem gives a biholomorphism \(f:\Omega\to\mathbb D\) with \(f(A)=0\); fixing \(f\prime(A)>0\) makes it unique. Corridor width alone does not determine \(\Omega\): its length, boundary shape and junctions are also needed for a particular numerical formula.
reconstruction: The topological hypotheses and derivative normalization are stated explicitly; no unseen corridor length is invented.
fate: This is the same established mapping theorem as in \citet{riemann1851grundlagen}. Thin corridors can make numerical conformal parametrization poorly conditioned, but the notes give no quantitative estimate to verify.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Existence and normalized uniqueness are settled. A unique explicit numerical map cannot be extracted from the incomplete geometric dimensions in the sketch.

title: A G-structure is a principal reduction
notes: The first definition takes a principal subbundle \(P\subset F(M)\) for \(G\subset GL(V)\), then says that G acts transitively on P.
statement: For a smooth n-manifold M and closed Lie subgroup \(G\subset GL(n,\mathbb R)\), a G-structure is a principal G-subbundle of its frame bundle. The right G-action is free and transitive on each fibre \(P_x\), not on all of P when the base has more than one point.
reconstruction: The word each fibre repairs the source statement.
fate: This is the standard definition recalled in \citet[Section~5.1]{alekseevskymichor1995cartan}; that later paper explicitly reviews older theory. The earlier index has the same reduction in1980-493.1.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Established; the global transitivity sentence is a faithful mathematical error in the notebook.

title: Tensor fields of constant algebraic type define reductions
notes: The examples include a metric, a tensor in one canonical form, an endomorphism with fixed Jordan form, an almost complex structure and a nondegenerate2-form.
statement: If a smooth tensor field takes values in one \(GL(n)\)-orbit and its adapted frames form a smooth reduction, its stabilizer is the structure group. A positive metric yields \(O(n)\); \(J^2=-I\) in dimension2m yields \(GL(m,\mathbb C)\); a nondegenerate alternating2-form yields \(Sp(2m,\mathbb R)\). An almost symplectic form becomes symplectic only with the additional differential condition \(d\omega=0\). An endomorphism requires locally constant algebraic type for its adapted frames.
reconstruction: The orbit/reduction smoothness and even-dimensional requirements are made explicit.
fate: These are the elementary G-structure examples in the framework of \citet[Section~5.1]{alekseevskymichor1995cartan}; the note itself distinguishes almost symplectic from symplectic.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Established. A pointwise tensor classification does not imply differential integrability of the resulting structure.

title: Equivalent description by a solder form
notes: The second definition gives a principal G-bundle with a V-valued1-form \(\theta\), equivariance, and kernel equal to the vertical tangent space. The equivalence is explained using coframes.
statement: For a faithful inclusion \(G\subset GL(V)\), a principal G-bundle \(P\to M\) with \(\dim M=\dim V\) and a horizontal equivariant form \(\theta\) satisfying \(\ker\theta_p=\ker d\pi_p\) determines a coframe \(T_xM\to V\) at each p over x. Equivariance \(R_g^*\theta=g^{-1}\theta\) makes these coframes a G-reduction, and conversely the tautological solder form of a reduction has these properties.
reconstruction: The quotient\textquotesingle s base space and the right-action convention are corrected.
fate: \citet[Section~5.1]{alekseevskymichor1995cartan} recalls precisely this solder-form formulation. It was established G-structure theory before1988.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The equivalence is standard. The quotient used in the notebook must be \(T_pP/T_p^vP\), which is canonically \(T_xM\).

title: First jets of sections as horizontal complements
notes: The first jet \(j_x^1s\) is identified with a right inverse of the projection derivative and with a horizontal subspace.
statement: For \(s(x)=p\), its first jet is determined by \(d s_x:T_xM\to T_pP\) with \(d\pi_p\circ d s_x=I\). Its image H complements the vertical space. Conversely every such linear splitting is realized by a local section to first order. At fixed p these splittings form an affine space modeled on \(\operatorname{Hom}(T_xM,\mathfrak g)\), identified with \(\operatorname{Hom}(V,\mathfrak g)\) using p.
fate: \citet[Section~6.1]{alekseevskymichor1995cartan} gives exactly the jet/horizontal-space identification, as recalled standard theory.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Established. This is the unrestricted first-jet bundle, before any torsion normalization defining a smaller prolongation.

title: A principal connection as an equivariant horizontal distribution
notes: The space of connections is written as the G-equivariant sections of \(P\prime\to P\); horizontal lifts give parallel transport along curves.
statement: A principal connection is a smooth G-equivariant assignment \(p\mapsto H_p\) with \(T_pP=H_p\oplus V_pP\). Equivalently it is a \(\mathfrak g\)-valued1-form \(\omega\) reproducing fundamental vertical fields and satisfying \(R_g^*\omega=\operatorname{Ad}(g^{-1})\omega\). The horizontal-lift ODE defines parallel transport along piecewise smooth paths in its existence interval; for principal connections it extends along compact parameter intervals by local trivializations.
fate: The principal-connection framework is recalled by \citet[Sections~2.6 and3]{alekseevskymichor1995cartan}. It is background, not a new canonical connection selected by every G-structure.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Established. The lecture defines the space of connections; it does not prove that torsion can always be set to zero.

title: The torsion function on the space of horizontal complements
notes: Using the vertical parallelism and \(\theta|_H:H\to V\), the notes define \(t(p\prime)(\xi,\eta)=d\theta((\theta|_H)^{-1}\xi,(\theta|_H)^{-1}\eta)\).
statement: For every horizontal complement H at p, this formula defines \(t(H)\in\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda^2V,V)\). For a selected connection, it is the coefficient function of the torsion2-form \(d\theta+\omega\wedge\theta\) evaluated on horizontal vectors. The alternating2-form, rather than an unrestricted bilinear map, is the natural target.
fate: \citet[Section~6.1]{alekseevskymichor1995cartan} records the same torsion function and its role in prolongation.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Standard construction. No invariant zero-torsion complement is guaranteed without an algebraic condition on the intrinsic torsion.

title: Change of horizontal complement and the Spencer alternation
notes: The final sentence asserts G-equivariance and \(G\prime=\operatorname{Hom}(V,\mathfrak g)\)-equivariance of torsion, without displaying the action on its target.
statement: If \(H_A\) is obtained from H by adding the fundamental vertical vector corresponding to \(A(v)\), then with right-action convention \(t(H_A)=t(H)-\delta A\), where \(\delta A(v,w)=A(v)w-A(w)v\). Thus the class in \(\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda^2V,V)/\delta\operatorname{Hom}(V,\mathfrak g)\) is independent of H. G acts linearly; the full space of changes of complement acts affinely by this alternation. The kernel of delta is the first algebraic prolongation.
reconstruction: The omitted action and its sign are supplied by the right-principal-bundle convention.
fate: \citet[Sections~6.1--6.2]{alekseevskymichor1995cartan} explicitly uses the Spencer map to normalize torsion and define prolongation.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Established after specifying the affine action and sign convention. The phrase equivariant alone does not mean torsion is invariant under all changes of connection.

title: A reading suggestion on thermodynamics and quasilinear equations
notes: Gelfand recommends his 1959 paper in Uspekhi, volume 14, issue 2, saying that three pages contain all thermodynamics.
statement: The identifiable reference is the 1959 exposition Some problems in the theory of quasi-linear equations, pp.~87--158. The remark recommends its thermodynamic discussion; it does not state a new theorem or identify a three-page passage precisely enough to extract one.
fate: \citet[publication record]{gelfand1959quasilinear} confirms the exact title, volume, pages and receipt on 17 November 1958. The full thermodynamic section was not read in this research.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The bibliographic identification is secure. The phrase all thermodynamics is an informal assessment, not an assertion of mathematical completeness.

title: Complete invariants of two planes in four dimensions
notes: Gelfand asks what should be called the angle between two two-dimensional planes in four-dimensional Euclidean space.
statement: For two linear two-planes \(U,W\) in a four-dimensional real inner-product space, choose orthonormal frame matrices \(Q_U,Q_W\). The singular values of \(Q_U^TQ_W\) are \(\cos\theta_1,\cos\theta_2\), where \(0\le\theta_1\le\theta_2\le\pi/2\). This ordered pair is a complete invariant under the full orthogonal group, and every pair in that range occurs.
reconstruction: The word planes is interpreted as linear subspaces and the acting group as the full orthogonal group, consistently with the following problem sheet.
fate: The singular-value characterization was already explicit in \citet[Section~3, Theorem~1]{bjorckgolub1973angles}, published in 1973. The earlier index records related angle questions in 1964-46.2. The same question is restated as problem 3 of record 737.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Solved classical finite-dimensional classification. One scalar angle loses information in this dimension.

title: Complete invariants of two closed Hilbert subspaces
notes: The second question asks for all invariants of a pair of subspaces in a Hilbert space.
statement: For an ordered pair of closed subspaces M,N of a real or complex Hilbert space, the four intersections \(M\cap N\), \(M\cap N^\perp\), \(M^\perp\cap N\), \(M^\perp\cap N^\perp\) contribute their Hilbert dimensions. On the remaining generic part \(K\oplus K\), the projections have forms \(P=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}I&0\\0&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) and \(Q=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}C^2&CS\\CS&S^2\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), where \(0<C<I\) means that C and \(S=(I-C^2)^{1/2}\) are injective positive contractions. Their endpoints may still belong to the continuous spectrum. The unitary or orthogonal equivalence class of C, together with the four dimensions, is complete.
reconstruction: Closedness, the full isometry group and the endpoint-kernel convention are supplied; these are essential for a projection-based answer.
fate: \citet[Theorems~1--3]{halmos1969subspaces} gives the two-projection canonical form and its completeness; the paper was received in April 1969. The statement is repeated and elaborated in record 737.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Solved for closed Hilbert subspaces. A mere set of spectral values is insufficient: spectral measure class and multiplicity are part of the invariant.

title: Formal Euclidean correlations from a local action
notes: The speaker writes correlation functions as \(Z^{-1}\int A_1(x_1)\cdots A_n(x_n)e^{-S[\varphi]}\mathcal D\varphi\), with \(S=\int\sigma(\varphi,\partial\varphi)\,d^2x\).
statement: This is a formal prescription for multilinear Euclidean correlation distributions. To make it a construction one must specify a measure or regularized limit, composite fields and coincident-point renormalization, and ensure \(0<Z<\infty\) when an ordinary normalization is used. The displayed continuum symbol \(\mathcal D\varphi\) alone does not provide these data.
reconstruction: Distributional interpretation and analytic existence conditions are supplied. The 1975 reconstruction source was checked at metadata/abstract level only.
fate: The established operator/correlation formulation is described by \citet[Introduction and Section~2]{belavinpolyakovzamolodchikov1984infinite}; a rigorous Euclidean reconstruction framework predates it in \citet[abstract]{osterwalderschrader1975euclidean}.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Established formal language, not a general existence theorem for every local action. Specific rigorously defined models require additional analytic input.

title: Operator products and recursive determination of correlations
notes: The fields form an algebra with \(A_i(x)A_j(y)=\sum_k c_{ij}^{\,k}(x,y)A_k(y)\). The notes say these coefficients and the one-point functions determine all correlations by repeated expansion; translation invariance makes the coefficients functions of \(x-y\).
statement: If the chosen field system has convergent OPE expansions in correlation functions on nested domains, and these expansions satisfy associativity, the OPE coefficients together with vacuum one-point functions determine higher correlation functions there by iteration and elsewhere by any justified analytic continuation. Formal expansions alone do not imply convergence or independence of the sequence of pairings.
reconstruction: The convergence domains and compatibility of repeated expansions are restored.
fate: \citet[Introduction, equation~(1.6)]{belavinpolyakovzamolodchikov1984infinite} explicitly formulates the OPE with convergence in a finite domain and associativity. This is background from 1984, not a result originating in the 1988 lecture.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Established under the stated OPE hypotheses. The notebook suppresses precisely the analytic and associativity conditions needed for the proposed recursion.

title: Stress tensor and the translation Ward identity
notes: A conserved symmetric field \(T^{\mu\nu}\) is required to generate the derivative of a field by a surrounding contour integral. The repeated formula contracts \(\varepsilon_{\mu\nu}\,dx^\lambda\).
statement:
A translation-generating stress tensor satisfies \(\partial_\mu T^{\mu
u}=0\) away from other insertions, with contact terms at insertions. With the normalization of the charge fixed, \(\oint T^{\mu
u}(x)A(y)\varepsilon_{\mu\lambda}\,dx^\lambda=\partial_{y^
u}A(y)\) expresses its action on a local field. Conservation justifies contour deformations avoiding other insertions.
reconstruction: The lambda contraction and the contact-term qualification repair the displayed identity.
fate: \citet[Section~2, equations~(2.1)--(2.10)]{belavinpolyakovzamolodchikov1984infinite} develops the stress-tensor Ward identity. The notation in the first notebook display has the correct free index; its repetition does not.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Standard Ward-identity construction. The literal repeated contraction is ill-formed, and conservation cannot be imposed without contact terms at coincident insertions.

title: Reflection positivity requires a full quadratic form
notes: For the reflection \(\vartheta(x^1,x^2)=(-x^1,x^2)\), the matrix \(\langle A_i^+(\vartheta x)A_j(x)\rangle\) is required to be positive definite for every x.
statement: The Euclidean positivity axiom is positive semidefiniteness of \(\langle(\Theta F)^*F\rangle\) for every finite linear combination F of smeared field products supported in one open time half-space. The reflected form can have null vectors, which are quotiented out in Hilbert-space reconstruction. Positivity of the displayed same-point matrix is only a restricted necessary test and does not by itself imply the full axiom.
reconstruction: The half-space, smearing, arbitrary finite sums and semidefinite quotient are missing in the notes.
fate: The opened record for \citet[abstract]{osterwalderschrader1975euclidean} confirms the corrected Euclidean reconstruction theorem; full-text retrieval was blocked, so no claim is made to have read that proof. The full quadratic-form condition is the explicit modern reconstruction used here.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Established framework. Strict pointwise positivity is too strong in the presence of null fields and too weak as a substitute for reflection positivity on all field products.

title: Construct substantive models of the field axioms
notes: After the algebra, symmetry and positivity requirements the speaker asks for meaningful examples of all this.
statement: A definite conformal version asks for a local two-dimensional theory with associative OPE, a stress tensor and a positive state space. The unitary Ising conformal theory supplies such a standard example, with central charge \(c=1/2\) and primary weights \((0,0),(1/2,1/2),(1/16,1/16)\) in its diagonal local sector. This is an example answering the request, not a classification of all models.
reconstruction: The Ising model is supplied as one precise response to the broad request. Section 6 of the cited paper gives its conformal weights and closed operator products.
fate: \citet[Section~6, equations~(6.11)--(6.18)]{belavinpolyakovzamolodchikov1984infinite} already develops degenerate theories and their correlation functions in 1984; the lecture is expository. The exact positivity completion of a continuum path integral is a separate analytic question.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The existence request had established nontrivial examples before the talk. The notebook does not state a definite universal classification problem.

title: Conservation and tracelessness give chiral stress components
notes: With \(z=x^1+ix^2\), the notebook defines \(T=T^{zz}\), \(\bar T=T^{\bar z\bar z}\), sets \(T^{z\bar z}=0\), then asserts \(\partial_{\bar z}T=\partial_z\bar T=0\).
statement: For a genuine contravariant symmetric tensor, \(T^{zz}=T^{11}-T^{22}+2iT^{12}\) and \(T^{z\bar z}=T^{11}+T^{22}\). Conservation and zero trace imply \(\partial_zT^{zz}=0\), so the displayed contravariant T has the opposite chirality. The conventional holomorphic component is the covariant \(T_{zz}=(T^{11}-T^{22}-2iT^{12})/4\), satisfying \(\partial_{\bar z}T_{zz}=0\). Rescaling this component gives the normalization used in the OPE.
reconstruction: This calculation distinguishes contravariant from covariant components rather than silently using the same symbol for both.
fate: The holomorphic stress-tensor construction is standard in \citet[Section~2, equations~(2.6)--(2.10)]{belavinpolyakovzamolodchikov1984infinite}. Direct tensor transformation and the two real conservation equations expose the notebook index inconsistency.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The standard chiral conclusion is correct after an explicit index/chirality correction. The separate equality \(T^{z\bar z}=T^\mu{}_\mu\) on P001433 is consistent with contravariant indices and \(ds^2=dz\,d\bar z\); it should not be independently changed by a factor of two.

title: Composite fields and the limits of Grassmann nilpotence
notes: The example lists electron and photon composites, says that powers \(\psi^5,\psi^6\) vanish because the spinor has four components, and then warns that a pointwise \(A^2\) need not exist.
statement: For four classical Grassmann generators at one point every homogeneous product of degree above four vanishes. This elementary exterior-algebra statement does not bound all quantum composites: derivatives give additional generators, and operator-valued distributions require a specified renormalized product. Even the product of two bosonic fields at the same point is not automatically defined.
reconstruction: The distinction between finite Grassmann generators and quantum local fields supplies the necessary scope.
fate: The field-system/OPE formulation of \citet[Introduction, equation~(1.6)]{belavinpolyakovzamolodchikov1984infinite} includes derivatives and composite fields. The finite Grassmann calculation is an elementary reconstruction, not a general theorem about electron-field operators.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The warning about coincident products is sound. The nilpotence assertion needs the restricted finite Grassmann-algebra interpretation; it is not an identity for every quantum spinor composite.

title: Contour modes of the stress tensor
notes: The modes are defined by \(\oint z^{n+1}T(z)A(w)\,dz/(2\pi i)\) on a contour around w; \(L_{-1}=\partial_w\) is then asserted.
statement: In a local coordinate \(t=z-w\), define \(L_n^{(w)}A(w)=\operatorname{Res}_{z=w}(z-w)^{n+1}T(z)A(w)\). The simple-pole Ward identity gives \(L_{-1}^{(w)}A=\partial_wA\). The global modes about the origin use \(z^{n+1}\); they act on fields at w by coordinate-dependent combinations and must be distinguished from local descendant modes.
reconstruction: The local/global coordinate distinction is made explicit.
fate: \citet[Section~2, equations~(2.18)--(2.21); Section~3]{belavinpolyakovzamolodchikov1984infinite} gives the contour generators and Laurent modes. The earlier occurrence 1982-573.17 records the same stress-tensor construction.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Established. The source formula is valid as a global charge expression, but the local highest-weight formulas later on require a coordinate centred at the insertion or an insertion at zero.

title: The singular stress-tensor operator product
notes: The Laurent expansion is assumed to start at order \(-4\); the coefficients are stated to be \(T_{-4}=cI/2\), \(T_{-3}=0\), \(T_{-2}=2T\), \(T_{-1}=\partial T\).
statement: For the normalized holomorphic stress tensor of an ordinary local CFT with a scalar central term and the conformal Ward identity, \[T(z)T(w)\sim\frac{c/2}{(z-w)^4}+\frac{2T(w)}{(z-w)^2}+\frac{\partial T(w)}{z-w}.\] The absence of a third-order pole and the scalar fourth-order coefficient use the stress-tensor transformation law and vacuum assumptions. Reflection positivity alone does not determine this OPE.
reconstruction: The notebook attributes more to positivity than it alone supplies; the Ward/vacuum assumptions are restored.
fate: The equivalent infinitesimal transformation with the Schwarzian central term is given in \citet[Section~2, equations~(2.12), (2.19)--(2.21)]{belavinpolyakovzamolodchikov1984infinite}, before this lecture.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Standard exact singular OPE under the stated CFT assumptions; regular terms contain further composite fields.

title: The two commuting Virasoro algebras
notes: The boxed formula is \([L_n,L_m]=(n-m)L_{n+m}+\frac c{12}(n^3-n)\delta_{n+m,0}\), and an antiholomorphic copy is described.
statement: Taking residues in the stress OPE yields the displayed commutator, with the central term multiplying the identity. The antiholomorphic modes satisfy the analogous relation, and left and right modes commute in the local theory. Modulo its centre this is the Witt algebra; integration of the central term requires a central extension or projective representation of the diffeomorphism group, not simply the unextended group.
reconstruction: The identity operator in the central term and the group-extension qualification are explicit.
fate: \citet[Section~2, equation~(2.21)]{belavinpolyakovzamolodchikov1984infinite} states precisely these relations. Prior occurrences include 1982-573.1 and 1985-657.1--4. No reducibility or singular-vector problem is posed in this passage, so the distinct earlier problem GP-1982-03 is not relabelled as a new problem here.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Established algebraic relation. The restriction to \(n=-1,0,1\) has zero central term and recovers the projective conformal subalgebra.

title: An asserted universal smallest length
notes: The speaker says that lengths below \(10^{-31}\) cm have no meaning, independently of theory, from relations among universal constants, and asks what space could mean with such a restriction.
statement: No axioms defining meaningful distance, observable localization or an admissible geometry are stated. A dimensional combination of constants gives a candidate scale; it does not by itself prove a lower bound on all measured distances or a theorem about spaces. Consequently no precise universal theorem can be reconstructed from this assertion.
reconstruction: No metric or observational definition is invented.
fate: The conformal-field-theory source \citet{belavinpolyakovzamolodchikov1984infinite} identifies the surrounding lecture but provides no identified result establishing this assertion. The search and source check did not identify an exact mathematical theorem behind it.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The literal philosophical/physical claim is not a definite mathematical open problem. The scanned exponent is retained; no updated numerical constant is substituted for it.

title: An unspecified adelic determinant algorithm
notes: The interjection says that some determinants are best computed by an adelic method.
statement: The determinant family, coefficient domain, input size, arithmetic-cost model and algorithm are all unspecified. Therefore the comparative claim best cannot be converted into a definite complexity theorem or numerical-analysis problem.
fate: The surrounding references to p-adic physics and the prior adelic lecture do not identify a particular determinant algorithm. Searches of the stated phrase and determinant/adelic terminology did not produce an exact attributable match.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Unidentified as a precise mathematical claim; neither an open-status judgment nor a claim of computational superiority is warranted.

title: A broad comparison of polygon and polyhedron theory
notes: The notes contrast complete knowledge of two-dimensional polyhedra with supposed little progress on three- and four-dimensional ones in two thousand years.
statement: The objects and questions are unspecified: convexity, combinatorial type, realizability, face enumeration and metric rigidity lead to different problems. The passage states no quantified theorem that can be assigned a precise present status.
fate: No exact problem is recoverable from the broad historical comparison. It is kept as a source remark rather than attached to an unrelated later polytope theorem.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Not identifiable as a specific research problem. This is not evidence that finite-dimensional polytope theory has had no development.

title: Coordinate variation and the conformal Ward identity
notes: Varying \(x^\mu\) by \(\varepsilon^\mu(x)\) gives a sum of field variations plus \(\int\partial_\mu\varepsilon_\nu\langle T^{\mu\nu}A_1\cdots A_n\rangle\). Integration by parts turns the variation into contours around insertions.
statement:
For separated insertions, a stress tensor satisfying the distributional Ward identity gives the stated contour action. If \(\partial_\mu\varepsilon_
u+\partial_
u\varepsilon_\mu=g(x)\delta_{\mu
u}\) and the stress tensor is symmetric and traceless, the bulk contraction vanishes away from insertions. Boundary terms, contact terms and any anomalies must be handled in the chosen theory; the unregularized path integral is only a motivation.
reconstruction: The contact and boundary terms omitted by the formal integration by parts are stated.
fate: \citet[Sections~2--3, especially equation~(3.4)]{belavinpolyakovzamolodchikov1984infinite} supplies the conformal Ward identities before the talk.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Established local derivation under the symmetry, regularity and boundary hypotheses. It does not establish conformal invariance for an arbitrary action.

title: Primary fields, descendants and conformal families
notes: Primaries satisfy \(L_n\phi=\bar L_n\phi=0\) for \(n>0\), \(L_0\phi=h\phi,\bar L_0\phi=\bar h\phi\), with \(h,\bar h\ge0\); the algebra is written as a direct sum of their descendant families.
statement: At the origin a highest-weight state has the displayed annihilation and eigenvalue conditions. Applying negative modes generates its highest-weight module, with null states quotiented out in an irreducible unitary family. In a unitary positive-energy theory \(h,\bar h\ge0\). A direct sum of such families requires an appropriate discrete semisimple spectrum; it is not automatic for every conformal theory or every noncompact model.
reconstruction: Coordinate origin, null-state quotient and the conditions for a direct-sum decomposition are supplied.
fate: \citet[Section~3, equations~(3.8)--(3.13)]{belavinpolyakovzamolodchikov1984infinite} presents primary fields and conformal families. The result predates this lecture.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Standard within the stated unitary highest-weight framework. The algebraic direct-sum sentence needs spectral/semisimplicity hypotheses, and the source does not pose a new singular-vector classification problem.

title: Scaling weights, spin and the identity field
notes: The identity has weights zero. Under \(z\mapsto\lambda z,\bar z\mapsto\bar\lambda z\), the notes assign the primary the factor \(\lambda^h\bar\lambda^{\bar h}\) and call \(h-\bar h\) its spin.
statement: The second coordinate must be \(\bar z\mapsto\bar\lambda\bar z\). For a primary, \(h+\bar h\) is its scaling dimension and \(h-\bar h\) its spin. In a passive coordinate-change convention \(\phi_{\rm new}(\lambda z,\bar\lambda\bar z)=\lambda^{-h}\bar\lambda^{-\bar h}\phi(z,\bar z)\); active conventions reverse this placement. The identity has \((h,\bar h)=(0,0)\).
reconstruction: The missing coordinate conjugation is a literal error; the sign of the transformation factor is a convention that the source leaves unstated.
fate: \citet[Introduction, equations~(1.16)--(1.17); Section~3]{belavinpolyakovzamolodchikov1984infinite} gives these transformation laws and weights.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Established after correcting the missing bar and specifying the active/passive convention. No sign correction of the weight factor is imposed without that convention.

title: An angle invariant for a line and a plane in three dimensions
notes: The preamble calls an angle a complete orbit invariant and asks for its attainable values. Problem 1 asks for the angle between a line and a plane in three-dimensional space, explicitly separating intersecting and nonintersecting cases.
statement: For an affine line \(\ell\) and an affine plane H under all Euclidean isometries, the direction angle \(\alpha\in[0,\pi/2]\), together with their distance \(\delta\ge0\), is complete, with the restriction \(\alpha>0\Rightarrow\delta=0\). When \(\alpha=0\), delta distinguishes a contained line from a disjoint parallel line. For linear subspaces only \(\delta=0\) occurs. Under origin-preserving orthogonal maps alone, additional positional data are needed for affine objects.
reconstruction: Allowing translations is an explicit interpretation of the nonintersecting case, not an unannounced change from the preamble about orthogonal maps.
fate: The directional angle is the elementary case of the singular-value characterization in \citet[Section~3, Theorem~1]{bjorckgolub1973angles}. The affine distance correction follows directly by moving the closest point or intersection to the origin.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Classical and solved after fixing the acting group. An angle alone is not a complete invariant of disjoint affine configurations.

title: An angle invariant for two planes in three dimensions
notes: Problem 2 asks for the angle between two planes in three-dimensional space.
statement: For linear two-planes U,W in \(\mathbb R^3\), their two principal angles are \(0,\theta\), with \(0\le\theta\le\pi/2\); theta is the acute angle between their normal lines and is a complete O(3) invariant. If affine planes are intended, distinct parallel planes additionally require their distance \(\delta>0\); nonparallel planes intersect, and their sole nonzero directional angle suffices under Euclidean isometries.
reconstruction: The linear and affine interpretations are separated.
fate: The linear statement is a dimension-three case of \citet[Section~3, Theorem~1]{bjorckgolub1973angles}. The affine supplement is elementary and is needed because the immediately preceding task includes disjoint affine objects.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Solved classical exercise. The source should not be read as claiming that one scalar classifies every origin-dependent affine placement.

title: Two principal angles classify two planes in four dimensions
notes: Problem 3 repeats the question about two two-dimensional subspaces of a four-dimensional inner-product space, without choosing coordinate axes.
statement: The complete O(4) invariant is \(0\le\theta_1\le\theta_2\le\pi/2\), with cosines the singular values of the cross-Gram matrix of orthonormal frames. Every such pair is realized by \(U=\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2)\) and \(W=\operatorname{span}(\cos\theta_1e_1+\sin\theta_1e_3,\cos\theta_2e_2+\sin\theta_2e_4)\).
fate: \citet[Section~3, Theorem~1]{bjorckgolub1973angles} gives the established singular-value formulation. This is the exact recurrence of 1987-735.2, with the range request supplied by the problem-sheet preamble.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Solved, including the full range of attainable invariants. The treatment for SO(4) requires the separate orientation discussion below.

title: A vector and a subspace require magnitude as well as direction
notes: Problem 4 gives \(v\in L\), a k-dimensional subspace V, and an inner product on the n-dimensional space L; it asks for their angle.
statement: Under O(L), a pair (v,V) is classified by \(n,k,\|P_Vv\|,\|P_{V^\perp}v\|\). For \(v\ne0\), these are equivalently the norm of v and the angle \(\alpha\) defined by \(\cos\alpha=\|P_Vv\|/\|v\|\). Every pair of nonnegative component norms is possible when \(0<k<n\); if k=0 the first is zero, and if k=n the second is zero. The zero vector is a separate orbit with no direction angle.
reconstruction: The source does not require a unit vector; its length is therefore retained.
fate: The projection formula is the rank-one case of \citet[Section~3]{bjorckgolub1973angles}; completeness follows by independently rotating the two orthogonal components.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Solved. The problem-sheet definition of a complete invariant makes normalization material: angle alone does not distinguish vectors of different lengths.

title: Finite-dimensional pairs: complete invariants and their exact range
notes: Problem 5 asks for the angle between subspaces V,W of dimensions k,m in an n-dimensional inner-product space.
statement: Let \(r=\min(k,m)\) and \(q=\max(0,k+m-n)\). The ordered principal angles \(0\le\theta_1\le\cdots\le\theta_r\le\pi/2\), with at least q zero entries, classify ordered pairs under O(n), or under U(n) in the complex version. Every list satisfying exactly these restrictions is attainable. The dimensions of the ambient space and of both subspaces are also part of the classification when they are not fixed.
reconstruction: The exact dimension-forced zero-angle condition supplies the range requested in the preamble.
fate: The cross-Gram SVD in \citet[Section~3, Theorem~1]{bjorckgolub1973angles} gives the principal angles. Orthogonal principal two-planes plus intersection and unmatched directions give both completeness and the stated dimension restriction.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Solved classical finite-dimensional problem, including attainability. Replacing the list by its minimum, maximum or average angle discards information.

title: One, two and three subspaces under the general linear group
notes: Problem 6 removes the inner product and asks for complete invariants of one subspace, a pair and an ordered triple, with GL(n) as the acting group.
statement: For one subspace the dimension suffices. For a pair, the dimensions of U,V and \(U\cap V\), together with n, suffice. Over \(\mathbb R\) or \(\mathbb C\), an ordered triple decomposes uniquely into eight one-dimensional membership types indexed by subsets of \(\{1,2,3\}\), and copies of the two-dimensional configuration of three distinct lines \(\operatorname{span}e_1,\operatorname{span}e_2,\operatorname{span}(e_1+e_2)\). The nine multiplicities are complete invariants. All nonnegative multiplicities occur, subject to the ambient dimension \(\sum_Sa_S+2b=n\) and any prescribed subspace dimensions.
reconstruction: The source omits the base field. The stated elementary decomposition is for real or complex vector spaces; its precise multiplicities answer the completeness and range requests.
fate: The introduction of \citet[Section~1]{gelfandponomarev1971quadruples} separates the easy r=2,3 cases from the four-subspace problem. The exact nine-type classification already appears in the prior index at 1972-277.5--6; it is established finite-type linear algebra, not a new 1988 conjecture.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Solved, with a discrete finite list of building-block types and arbitrary admissible multiplicities. Pairwise intersection dimensions alone do not capture the two-dimensional triple block.

title: Two lines in the Minkowski plane
notes: Problem 7 fixes the quadratic form \(-x_1^2+x_2^2\) and asks for complete invariants of two lines under its preserving group.
statement: For coincident lines the causal type (negative, positive, null) is complete. For two distinct unoriented lines choose nonzero spanning vectors u,v and form \(G=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\langle u,u\rangle&\langle u,v\rangle\\\langle u,v\rangle&\langle v,v\rangle\end{smallmatrix}\right)\). Its equivalence class under \(G\mapsto DGD\), with invertible real diagonal D, is a complete O(1,1) invariant. The attainable matrices are precisely the symmetric two-by-two matrices of signature (1,1), equivalently determinant less than zero. This formulation includes null lines without division by their zero norms.
reconstruction: The diagonal rescaling identifies lines rather than chosen vectors; no orientation or time-orientation constraint is imposed.
fate: This two-dimensional answer follows directly by sending the basis (u,v) to another basis with the same Gram matrix. It is a simple case of the broader form-preserving classification later treated by \citet[Introduction and Theorem~1]{sergeichuk1990pairs}; the elementary case was already available before the talk.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Solved. An ordinary cosine alone cannot cover spacelike, timelike and null cases.

title: Pairs in finite-dimensional indefinite and degenerate forms
notes: Problem 8 extends the pair problem to higher Minkowski dimensions, arbitrary indefinite signature, and degenerate forms such as \(x_1^2+x_2^2\) on \(\mathbb R^3\).
statement: Fix a finite-dimensional vector space over a field of characteristic different from two with a symmetric, skew-symmetric or Hermitian form F, allowing degeneracy, and two labelled subspaces. Classify triples \((V_F;U_1,U_2)\) up to form-preserving linear isomorphisms carrying each labelled subspace to its counterpart. Sergeichuk gives a complete canonical decomposition for this problem, up to the classification of the Hermitian forms over the relevant fields; for the real symmetric setting these residual forms are determined by their inertia. Isometry blocks, their multiplicities and their allowed field parameters are the complete data, rather than only ordinary principal-angle numbers.
reconstruction: The field, form type, labelled nature and isometry category are fixed explicitly. The notebook asks only the real symmetric cases; the cited theorem treats a broader family.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1]{sergeichuk1990pairs} supplies a precise later classification covering the finite-dimensional indefinite and degenerate formulations. The paper was received on 13 September 1988 and published in 1990; its introduction mentions a partial earlier announcement, so this date is not asserted as the first discovery of every component.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The finite-dimensional problem has a canonical-form solution. The opened result does not settle the subsequent infinite-dimensional indefinite version, and no such extrapolation is made.

title: Passing from the full orthogonal group to the special group
notes: After the indefinite variants the sheet asks that all listed problems be considered for both O(n) and SO(n).
statement: For a nondegenerate real quadratic space, an O-orbit splits into two SO-orbits exactly when the stabilizer has no determinant-minus-one element; this follows because SO has index two. In the Euclidean ordered-pair case, it splits exactly when all four intersections \(U\cap W,U\cap W^\perp,U^\perp\cap W,U^\perp\cap W^\perp\) vanish. Equivalently, \(n=2k=2m\) and every principal angle lies strictly between zero and \(\pi/2\). Otherwise a reflection in one of those intersections keeps the orbit unsplit. For a degenerate form the full preserving group can have arbitrary nonzero determinant on its radical, so this index-two argument cannot simply be transferred.
reconstruction: The stabilizer criterion and the degeneracy caveat are supplied; the latter prevents an incorrect universal two-orbit claim.
fate: The criterion is an elementary index-two orbit calculation, with the Euclidean stabilizer read from the principal-angle blocks of \citet[Section~3]{bjorckgolub1973angles}. The invariant is augmented by a binary orientation choice exactly in the split case.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Solved for the stated nondegenerate groups. The notation O(n),SO(n) in the degenerate extension needs a definition and cannot be used to infer an index-two subgroup there.

title: Four subspaces under GL: the Gelfand--Ponomarev classification
notes: Problem 9 asks for complete invariants of a quadruple of subspaces and explicitly calls it the content of the work of Gelfand and Ponomarev.
statement: For an ordered quadruple in a finite-dimensional vector space over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, decomposition into indecomposable quadruples reduces the classification to the discrete families and one-parameter families listed by Gelfand--Ponomarev. With defect \(d=\sum_i\dim U_i-2\dim V\), indecomposable defects are \(-2,-1,0,1,2\); the continuous regular families have defect zero. Their block multiplicities and parameters give complete invariants. Real versions require real canonical blocks rather than silently assuming every eigenvalue is real.
reconstruction: The algebraically closed characteristic-zero hypothesis is the one actually read in the original paper. The labelled order of the four subspaces is retained.
fate: \citet[Section~2, Assertions~1--2; Section~3, Theorem~1]{gelfandponomarev1971quadruples} gives the explicit list and decomposition. It was received on 21 October 1970 and published in 1971. Earlier occurrences are 1970-198.1--13 and 1972-277.7.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Solved before the talk. The source explicitly attributes existing work; it is not an open classification request in the historical sense.

title: Principal angles of the two tensor subspaces
notes: Problem 10, attributed to A. A. Kirillov junior, gives an inner-product space L, tensors \(a,b\in L\otimes L\), and asks for the angle between \(a\otimes L\) and \(L\otimes b\) in \(L^{\otimes3}\). The preamble explicitly asks which invariant values are attainable.
statement: For a finite-dimensional real or complex Hilbert space of dimension d and nonzero tensors a,b, write their coefficient matrices as A,B in one orthonormal basis. The d principal cosines are the singular values of \((\overline A B)^T/(\|A\|_F\|B\|_F)\). If d is at least two, the complete range is all ordered \(s_1\ge\cdots\ge s_d\ge0\) with \(\sum_js_j\le1\). If d=1 the only cosine is 1. Zero tensors change the subspace dimensions and are excluded from this d-angle statement.
reconstruction: Finite dimension, nonzero tensors and normalization are explicit additions. The real source case is covered; the complex Hilbert variant is also stated. The complete range proof is the chapter annotation, not a result claimed to be in the 1973 paper.
fate: The singular-value interpretation is an application of the established principal-angle theorem of \citet[Section~3, Theorem~1]{bjorckgolub1973angles}. The chapter annotation at Section~\ref{dev:tensor-angles} proves the normalized cross-Gram formula and the exact range directly. It is an explicit solution of this finite-dimensional exercise, with no claim of novelty.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Solved in the stated finite-dimensional reconstruction, including attainable values. The source only says inner-product space; finite dimension is inferred from its placement before the separate Hilbert-space section, and is recorded rather than hidden.

title: Hilbert pairs, discrete angles and continuous spectral data
notes: Problem 11 asks for a complete invariant of two Hilbert subspaces and for examples with a countable set or a continuum of angle values.
statement: For closed M,N, use the four intersection dimensions and the generic positive contraction C from 1987-735.3. On a separable Hilbert space its spectral measure class together with multiplicity gives the full continuous invariant.
